'''George Adomian''' (1922 – June 17, 1996)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=MATLAB TUTORIAL for the First Course: Adomian Decomposition|url=https://www.cfm.brown.edu/people/dobrush/am33/Matlab/intro/adomian.html|website=www.cfm.brown.edu|access-date=2025-11-30|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cfm.brown.edu/people/dobrush/am33/image/Adomian.pdf|title=Dr George Adomian – distinguished scientist and mathematician|date=1996|access-date=30 November 2025|website=www.cfm.brown.edu|last=Rach|first=R. C.}}</ref> was an American [[list of mathematicians|mathematician]], aerospace engineer, and academic of Armenian descent.<ref name=":0" /> He developed the [[Adomian decomposition method]] (ADM) for solving [[nonlinear differential equation]]s, both ordinary and partial.<ref name=":1" /> The method is explained, among other places, in his book ''Solving Frontier Problems in Physics: The Decomposition Method'' (Kluwer, Dordrecht, 2004).<ref name="obit">{{cite news |title=Dr. George Adomian |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159061364/?article=cadd4949-1f20-46ef-a00b-5d1a71d17b39&focus=0.4960462,0.19715154,0.6108493,0.3864087&xid=3355 |access-date=May 3, 2024 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=June 22, 1996 |page=16 |language=en}}</ref>

He was educated at [[Cass Technical High School]] in Detroit. He earned a bachelor's and master's of science in electrical engineering at the [[University of Michigan]] and a PhD in physics from [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]]<ref name="obit" /> in 1961, advised by [[David Saxon]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=George Adomian - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=4980|website=www.mathgenealogy.org|access-date=2025-11-30}}</ref> His dissertation was titled ''Linear Stochastic Operators''.<ref name=":2" />

He was a professor at [[Pennsylvania State University]] from 1964-66, and then was Chair of Applied Mathematics at the [[University of Georgia]] (UGA) from 1966 through 1989. While at UGA, he started the [[Center for Applied Mathematics]].<ref name="obit" />

He was a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name=":1" /> He was also a member of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], [[American Mathematical Society]], [[American Physical Society]], [[Sigma Xi]], [[Tau Beta Pi]], [[Eta Kappa Nu]], and [[Sigma Pi Sigma]].<ref name=":1" />

==Selected works==
* G. Adomian: ''Stochastic Systems'', Academic Press, 1983. {{ISBN|0-12-044370-8}}
* G. Adomian: ''Nonlinear Stochastic Operator Equations'', Academic Press, 1986. {{ISBN|0-12-044375-9}}
* G. Adomian: ''Nonlinear Stochastic Systems Theory and Applications to Physics'', Kluwer Academic Publishers, 1989. {{ISBN|90-277-2525-X}}
